bug_report_content: {"id":103,"status":"Fixed","summary":"$super is replaced when it should not be replaced","labels":["Type-Defect","Priority-Medium"],"stars":1,"commentCount":12,"comments":[{"id":0,"commenterId":-7686483319032304251,"content":"What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Have javascript using prototype's $super 2. Compile with advanced_optimizations 3. See that $super is replaced by for example $super$$4 What is the expected output? What do you see instead? $super should not be renamed as it is used by prototype. What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? Latest from svn. Please provide any additional information below. Personally I made a quick fix in MakeDeclaredNamesUnique.java line 79: if (t.getCompiler().getCodingConvention().isExported(name)) { continue; } This fixed it for me, but not sure if that's the right place or method to solve this, as I am unfamiliar with the project.","timestamp":1265486639,"attachments":[]},{"id":1,"commenterId":436477103612417078,"content":"Quick question: Are you building from the command line, or using Closure Compiler programmatically? What does your command line to the compiler look like?","timestamp":1265650854,"attachments":[]},{"id":2,"commenterId":-7686483319032304251,"content":"Comment deleted","timestamp":1265657369,"attachments":[]},{"id":3,"commenterId":-7686483319032304251,"content":"I am building from the command line, here's what the command looks like: java -jar /Users/jochen/closure/build/compiler.jar --compilation_level ADVANCED_OPTIMIZATIONS --js share.js --module share:1 --js main.js --module main:1 --js recording.js --module recording:1 --js comments.form.js --module commentsform:1 --js facebook.share.js --module facebookshare:1 --externs prototype.js --module_output_path_prefix /Users/jochen/ruby/karaoke/public/javascripts/compiled/","timestamp":1265657398,"attachments":[]},{"id":4,"commenterId":436477103612417078,"content":"That looks like the right fix. Want to add a test case, and submit the change to the project? (Hint: the tests run in the Google coding convention, so a leading underbar is the sign of an exported name.)","timestamp":1265683182,"attachments":[]},{"id":5,"commenterId":1948758734812428220,"content":"What is the effect of the change? $super needs to be unique during the name normalization or this would break inlining right?","timestamp":1265685912,"attachments":[]},{"id":6,"commenterId":-7699928860083865744,"content":"how does $super work again? wouldn't it be impossible to inline the function anyway, because it uses crazy reflection?","timestamp":1265690359,"attachments":[]},{"id":7,"commenterId":-5060162230523776870,"content":"I feel a uncomfortable with breaking the normalization for this. I would prefer to special case the renaming to look for "$super$..." and change this back to "$super" since we are already special casing it there to prevent it from being renamed in the first place. If it were to be inlined it would become (currently) something like JSCompiler_inline_$super... so would be broken regardless of the normalization so I would assume this doesn't happen but someone should check.","timestamp":1265698723,"attachments":[]},{"id":8,"commenterId":436477103612417078,"content":"If the first parameter of a method on a class object is $super, Prototype's code for setting up the class (in addMethod) inserts a reference to the superclass. Here's the relevant code: Class.Methods { addMethods: function(source) { var ancestor = this.superclass && this.superclass.prototype; var properties = Object.keys(source); ... for (var i = 0, length = properties.length; i < length; i++) { var property = properties[i], value = source[property]; if (ancestor && Object.isFunction(value) && value.argumentNames().first() == "$super") { .... Alan added a change in November to avoid renaming $super by marking it as an exported symbol in the DefaultCodingConvention. To correctly compile Prototype code in advanced mode, we'll need to make sure the setup code for the class correctly does the parameter substitution. See http://www.prototypejs.org/assets/2008/9/29/prototype-1.6.0.3.js http://www.prototypejs.org/api/class/create","timestamp":1265737420,"attachments":[]},{"id":9,"commenterId":-5060162230523776870,"content":"To make my comment clear, one of the points of the normalization is to make it easier for passes if the "x" they saw is the same "x" they saw earlier (without needing to track scope). This makes things much easier for code motion because you don't need to worry about masking a variable of the same name. If you change it "$super" is not unique the results would be unpredictable. After renaming it doesn't matter if the name is unique as the normalization is expected as renaming by design creates as many non-unique names as possible.","timestamp":1265828899,"attachments":[]},{"id":10,"commenterId":-5060162230523776870,"content":"","timestamp":1268446071,"attachments":[]},{"id":11,"commenterId":-7699928860083865744,"content":"This issue was closed by revision r139.","timestamp":1268779995,"attachments":[]}]}
